questions.q: The fundamental objective of public sector accounting is to
options: Maximize net operational profit and distribute regular dividends to citizens
Ensure stewardship, accountability, and transparency in the receipt and disbursement of public funds for social welfare
Determine the exact net asset value per share of state-owned entities
Minimize government tax collection in order to maximize private individual savings
questions.explain: Unlike private sector accounting which primarily aims at measuring **profitability** and wealth maximization for owners, **public sector accounting** focuses on **stewardship, budgetary control, accountability, and transparency** in using public funds to provide public goods and services.

questions.q: Traditional government accounting relies predominantly on the **cash basis of accounting** because it
options: Accurately applies the matching and accrual concepts across distinct accounting years
Focuses on budgetary compliance by recording transactions only when actual cash is received or disbursed
Eliminates the possibility of government budget deficits occurring
Provides an exact calculation of annual depreciation on public infrastructure like highways and bridges
questions.explain: The traditional **cash basis of accounting** in government records transactions only when physical cash is received or payments are actually made. Its primary advantage in the public sector is ensuring strict **budgetary control**, verifying that actual cash spending does not exceed the legal appropriations approved by the legislature.
